summary: Intermittent GPU supply continuity failure causing queued-batch backpressure and P99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring spikes in request queue length and p99 latency on their dedicated pool during midday window. Symptoms appear as sustained queued-batches, autoscaler failing to return capacity quickly, and transient 5xx responses when fallback routing engages.

Impact:
- ChorusAI experiences degraded inference throughput for 2 of their mission-critical routes (chat and batch-translate).
- User-facing latency p99 rose from ~150ms to 3.2s during peak and occasional 5xx errors.
- Customer SLAs for dedicated contract at risk.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ChorusAI-reserved-usw2-1
- Region: us-west-2
- Node type: 8xA100-80GB equivalent (heterogeneous mix of A100 + older V100 nodes in pool)
- Redwood runtime version: 2026.02.18

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run steady traffic patterned as ChorusAI production: 20 RPS short chat streams + periodic large-embedding jobs (100 reqs/min).
2) Observe autoscaler behavior during 11:45–12:30 window (customer's peak).
3) Monitor cluster GPU allocation, pod evictions, and queue length.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler fails to allocate additional GPU-backed slots quickly; new allocations report "allocation pending" for 90–180s intermittently.
- Several older V100 nodes show sustained 95% memory pressure, evicting batches and causing batch serialization.
- Prefix KV cache retention grows for active chat sessions and causes memory fragmentation on some nodes.
- When autoscaler fallback triggers, requests are routed to a lower-throughput variant resulting in 5xx on first few requests.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add capacity within configured warm-up window (<=30s) and avoid evictions that cause p99 jumps.

Attached logs and dashboards:
- link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/cluster/chrousai-dedicated?orgId=5
- support logs excerpt: /var/log/redwood/support/SUP-738264/chunked-alloc.log
comments: 2026-03-01 09:22 - Support (Aisha): Customer opened with p99 spikes and queued-batch growth during peak. Asked for immediate logs and pool id.
2026-03-01 09:45 - SRE (Diego): Scoped to dedicated pool ChorusAI-reserved-usw2-1. Observed allocation lag and heterogenous node mix. Collecting GPU daemon logs and autoscaler metrics.
2026-03-01 10:12 - Customer (ChorusAI - ops): We see timeouts around 11:50 but then recovery after 2-3 minutes. This is causing a small percent of failed jobs. Requesting priority fix.
2026-03-01 12:05 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced queue growth in lab with traffic replay. Noted NVLink errors and kernel retries on older V100 nodes. Temporarily drained aged nodes from pool as mitigation.
2026-03-02 08:30 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed reduction in failures after drain, but p99 still elevated during next peak. Requesting deeper kernel-level analysis and autoscaler tuning.

2026-03-03 15:20 - Eng (Maya Lin): Submitted hypothesis that KV cache growth + smaller-memory nodes cause fragmentation and longer-than-expected warmup. Preparing a patch to gate large-KV sessions to larger-memory nodes.

2026-03-03 16:05 - SRE (Diego): Scheduled controlled rollout: 1) pin critical routes to larger-memory nodes, 2) adjust autoscaler scale-up aggressiveness for this pool, 3) enable temporary request-shedding threshold to avoid 5xx cascade.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor - one tenant running heavy embedding sweeps created sustained memory pressure that prevented new batch placements on some nodes.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler backoff logic mis-triggered due to intermittent node registration flaps (seen as several 503/timeout events from provisioner).
Metrics observed: queue_length increased from baseline 6 -> 72 during peak; p99 latency correlated with queued-batches. GPU allocation pending spikes correspond to cloud API rate-limit 429s at times.
Logs: nvml reports memory fragmentation warnings on V100 nodes (nvml_errors.log). Some pods on V100 reported OOMKill of sidecar checkpoint writer, causing background IO noise.
Related config: pool has mix: 60% A100, 40% V100 (legacy). Allocation logic currently treats nodes as fungible; need affinity for memory-heavy sessions.

Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/cluster/allocations -> spike visual for 2026-03-01 11:40-12:10; correlate with cloud provider quota messages: https://provider.console/ops/quotas/region/us-west-2
root_cause: A combination of noisy neighbor workload (large embedding sweep) causing sustained memory pressure on lower-memory V100 nodes, plus autoscaler's conservative backoff in response to transient provisioner rate-limits. This led to allocation pending states, which created queued-batch backpressure and p99 latency spikes.
resolution: Short term (mitigation): 2026-03-01 13:00 - drained V100 subset from the dedicated pool for ChorusAI to force allocation to A100 nodes. Adjusted autoscaler scale-up cooldown to 20s for this pool. Enabled request-shedding at queue_length>60 to prevent cascade into 5xx.

Medium term (next 2 weeks): Implement node-affinity gating so large-KV/embedding workloads preferentially land on high-memory nodes. Add autoscaler tweak to ignore transient 429s from cloud provider for 60s before applying backoff multiplier.

Long term (postmortem action): Replace legacy V100 nodes in this reserved pool or reserve a homogeneous A100-only subset for memory-heavy tenants. Add monitoring alert for KV cache growth per-tenant and an automated mitigation playbook. Owner: SRE (Diego) + Runtime Eng (Maya).
Customer communication: Sent customer a summary of mitigations and timeline. Offered additional dedicated capacity while pool is rebalanced.
